name: CA-23
label: Likely R

key_factors: Prediction markets price Democratic chances near 6%
No public polling of the race
model.rationale: The district's 9-point Republican lean, Obernolte's incumbency and roughly 18-to-1 fundraising edge over Tessa Lynn Hodge, and prediction markets pricing Democratic odds near 6% all point to a comfortable Republican hold. With no polls or expert ratings available, the forecast stays close to the fundamentals.
model.watch: A late surge of Democratic outside spending or a top-two matchup shift could narrow the margin, but the structural lean makes an upset unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Republican incumbent Jay Obernolte seeks re-election in a California district that leans about nine points Republican, and he advanced to the general election as the favorite. He has raised roughly $1.5 million and holds over $1.6 million in cash, while Democratic challenger Tessa Lynn Hodge has raised under $100,000 with minimal outside support. Prediction markets give Democrats only about a 6% chance, and no expert raters list the race as competitive.

The forecast expects Obernolte to win by roughly nine to ten points, consistent with the district's partisan baseline. Without public polling, uncertainty is somewhat elevated, but the combination of lean, incumbency, and money makes a Democratic upset a low-probability outcome.
